updates.name: Randall K. Kolka
updates.bio: Randy Kolka is a Research Soil Scientist with the USDA Forest Service Northern Research Station and adjunct faculty in Forest Resources at the University of Minnesota. He studies how forest, agricultural and urban land management alter water, carbon, nutrient and mercury cycling, including carbon pools and emissions in peatlands.
updates.research_interests: land-management effects on nutrient, carbon, mercury and water cycling; peatland carbon pools and emissions; forestry best management practices in riparian and wetland systems; perennial vegetation in agricultural watersheds; stream restoration and nutrient cycling
updates.current_affiliation: USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station

updates.name: Reed Bowman
updates.bio: Reed Bowman (died 2023) was an ornithologist at Archbold Biological Station from 1991, eventually becoming its first endowed Fitzpatrick Program Director for Avian Ecology before retiring in 2023 as Emeritus Research Biologist. For three decades he studied Florida Scrub-Jays and guided conservation of that species plus Red-cockaded Woodpeckers and Florida Grasshopper Sparrows.
updates.research_interests: Florida Scrub-Jay ecology and conservation; Red-cockaded Woodpecker and Florida Grasshopper Sparrow conservation; prescribed-fire requirements of Florida Scrub-Jays, Red-cockaded Woodpeckers and Florida Grasshopper Sparrows; behavioral, evolutionary and landscape ecology; ecological genetics; endocrinology; conservation biology

updates.name: Richard A. Feely
updates.bio: Richard Feely is a Senior Scientist at NOAA's Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory in Seattle and an affiliate full professor of oceanography at the University of Washington. A chemical oceanographer trained at Texas A&M, he investigates the ocean carbon cycle, the processes governing oceanic uptake and release of anthropogenic CO2, and ocean acidification effects on marine ecosystems.
updates.research_interests: ocean carbon cycling; ocean acidification; sources and sinks of anthropogenic CO2 in the ocean; impacts of CO2 on marine ecosystems

updates.bio: Robert Gleason is Center Director of the USGS Northern Prairie Wildlife Research Center, located in Jamestown, North Dakota. His USGS profile lists expertise in greenhouse-gas fluxes and organic carbon, and his work includes Prairie Pothole Region studies of wetland management, climate and bird communities and of brine contamination from Williston Basin energy development.

updates.name: Robert A. Slesak
updates.bio: Robert A. Slesak is a Research Forester with the USDA Forest Service Pacific Northwest Research Station. His recent Treesearch publications address long-term soil productivity installations, logging-debris and vegetation-control effects on Douglas-fir, reforestation spacing and assisted migration, and underplanting replacement species in Minnesota black ash wetlands at risk from emerald ash borer.

updates.name: Robert A. Weller
updates.bio: Robert Weller is a part-time Senior Scientist in Physical Oceanography at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, previously chairing that department and leading a NOAA cooperative institute focused on climate and oceans. He studies air-sea interaction and upper-ocean response to atmospheric forcing, develops current meters and surface meteorological instruments, and has co-chaired OceanSITES and U.S. CLIVAR.
updates.research_interests: wind-forced upper-ocean motion; mixed-layer dynamics; upper-ocean velocity structure; air-sea interaction and fluxes; current meters and surface meteorological instrumentation; global ocean observing system

updates.name: Robert B. Waide
updates.bio: Robert B. Waide is Professor Emeritus of Biology at the University of New Mexico, with a Wisconsin PhD in zoology. His work covers long-term population and trophic dynamics in tropical ecosystems, biodiversity-ecosystem function links, land-cover effects on regional climate, disturbance along abiotic gradients, and remote-sensing estimates of biodiversity.
updates.research_interests: long-term population dynamics of tropical organisms; trophic dynamics in tropical ecosystems; biodiversity and ecosystem function; land-use and land-cover change effects on regional climate; abiotic gradients, disturbance and ecosystem structure; remote sensing of biodiversity

updates.name: Robert F. Chen
updates.bio: Robert F. (Bob) Chen is a UMass Boston professor in its School for the Environment, where he also serves as Director of Grant Scholarly Initiatives in the Provost's Office. A Scripps-trained chemical oceanographer, he studies coastal carbon biogeochemistry, chromophoric dissolved organic matter, salt-marsh carbon export, and coastal sensor networks, and leads ocean-science education projects.

updates.name: Robert M. Hirsch
updates.bio: Robert M. Hirsch is an emeritus research hydrologist with the USGS Water Resources Mission Area, which he joined in 1976. He was acting USGS Director in 1993-94 and Chief Hydrologist from 1994 to 2008, then returned to research on long-term streamflow and water-quality change, developing the WRTDS method and EGRET R package. He retired in 2018.
updates.research_interests: trends in streamflow; long-term change in surface-water quality; Weighted Regressions on Time, Discharge, and Season (WRTDS); EGRET R package for river trend analysis; statistical methods in water resources; floods and droughts
